capabilities.title: Memoz task flow
capabilities.description: Find the active task from the project's .memoz/tasks.json declaration and work on exactly one. Use when starting, continuing or closing work in a project tracked with Memoz. Never guesses where work lives.

capabilities.title: Memoz closure writer
capabilities.description: Write the closure record when a piece of work finishes: what changed, decisions and rejected options, measurements with their conditions, falsified assumptions, and criteria that could not be closed. Use when finishing a task, sub-task or release. Refuses to close on a missing field.

capabilities.title: Memoz recurring-mistake log
capabilities.description: Record a mistake that has happened before, in one place, with a count. Use when something that just went wrong feels familiar. Asks whether it is a new shape or another occurrence rather than deciding alone.

capabilities.title: Memoz mutation discipline
capabilities.description: Verify that a new test actually locks what it claims: break the code on purpose and watch it fail. Use after adding a test for a specific defect. Distinguishes died, survived and not-applied — the last is not a result.

capabilities.title: Memoz decision record
capabilities.description: Record a decision together with the options rejected and the ground each was rejected on, plus what observation would reopen it. Use when a choice is made that outlives the task.

capabilities.title: Memoz measurement record
capabilities.description: Record a number with the conditions that produced it and what it does not show. Use when benchmarking or measuring anything that will be quoted later.

capabilities.title: Memoz friction record
capabilities.description: Record what got in the way while using something: goal, what happened, what you expected, the workaround, and the decision. Use at the moment of friction, not at the end of the session.

capabilities.title: Memoz brainstorming
capabilities.description: Work out what is wanted before building it: search the knowledge layer for prior decisions, find the intent under the request, widen the options, name the constraint that decides it, and stop at a decision record. Use before implementing a feature or picking an approach.

capabilities.title: Memoz systematic debugging
capabilities.description: Find a defect by elimination and keep what the elimination taught: search the knowledge layer first, reproduce before explaining, write hypotheses down before testing them, never conclude from absence, distrust the instrument, and prove the cause by putting the bug back. Use on any failure whose cause is not obvious.

capabilities.title: Memoz verification before completion
capabilities.description: Produce the evidence before claiming a piece of work is done, fixed or working: state the claim, run the thing that would disprove it, confirm the tooling actually ran, and report what remains unverified. Use before finishing work, committing, or reporting a result.

capabilities.title: Memoz planning
capabilities.description: Break understood work into pieces that can be closed one at a time, each with a completion criterion you can actually run, plus the exclusions and the open questions. Use after the approach is settled and before implementing.

capabilities.title: Memoz parallel work
capabilities.description: Orchestrate several pieces of work at once: one worktree, branch and task note per piece; check file overlap and ask before running overlapping work in parallel; start implementer and independent reviewer agents; re-verify every claim yourself; merge shared hot files in order and always regenerate them. Use when splitting work across agents or worktrees.

agents.title: Memoz implementer
agents.description: Implements one piece of work in its own worktree and writes its report into the task note. Use when an orchestrator hands off a single piece; the task note, branch and owned files are given in the prompt. Does not push, merge or change task status.

agents.title: Memoz reviewer
agents.description: Reviews one branch's diff independently and adversarially, asking what contract the change breaks that the compiler and tests cannot see. Use after an implementer finishes and before the orchestrator asks a human to approve. Does not change code; never reads the task note before forming its own view.
